start_here: Say to your AI: "Work out how this device of mine stands (caught up, offline or still holding changes) as the device list to keep", with {"device_id":"d-sample01","state":"caught-up","now":"2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z"}. It runs tool:say-how-this-device-stands and answers {"device":{"device_id":"d-sample01","title":"","kind":"","state":"caught-up","waiting":0,"seen_at":"2026-01-01T00:00:00.000Z"},"written":true}
no_lists_because: It names no list of yours and keeps nothing: the device rows come in with the request and the next device list comes back for your AI to keep.
instructions: 1. Say to your AI: "Work out how this device of mine stands (caught up, offline or still holding changes) as the device list to keep", and give it device_id; state.
2. The AI calls run_resource_operation at @workshop-tools with method tools:run, tool tool:say-how-this-device-stands and its input (the worked example shows one).

3. Read what comes back: Reads and keeps nothing. Takes one device's report: device_id (the id the device keeps for itself), state, waiting (the changes it still holds), at (when its writes last reached your store), title, kind and copy_id (the copy of your records it keeps), with your device rows as devices. Answers the report as the next device list (devices) for you to keep, and written: true; the list changes only when what you would see changed, or when the device's last catch-up moved by more than an hour; at most 40 devices are kept, newest first. When nothing changed it answers written: false and no list.
4. It reads and writes no rows: everything it works from is in the request.
